core.title: Draw component events only from the owning feature's ioSeeds
core.given: A component belonging to a feature declares consumed or produced events, or dependencies
core.when: the planner authors, edits or reviews those events or dependencies, or changes the feature's ioSeeds
core.then: Every declared consumed event must come from feature.ioSeeds.consume and fit the component's role, and every declared produced event from feature.ioSeeds.produce and fit its capability, so all events are a subset of, and traceable to, a feature ioSeed.
prefer: Need a new event? Add it to the feature's ioSeeds first, then reference it.
Pick only the ioSeeds events the component's role actually consumes / its capability actually produces; the filter selects, it does not force inclusion of every seed.
avoid: Inventing inputs/outputs the feature never declared (e.g. producing an event absent from ioSeeds.produce).
Events not selected by the role (consume) or capability (produce) filter.
More than 3 consumed or 3 produced events per component.
Dependencies other than same-feature components or external dependencies.
core.why: Limiting component events to the feature's ioSeeds keeps each component's interface within its feature's declared contract, so no component invents inputs or outputs the feature never promised.
evidence: For each component, set(consumes) is a subset of the owning feature.ioSeeds.consume and set(produces) a subset of feature.ioSeeds.produce.
Each consumed event is justified by the component's role and each produced event by its capability (filtered from the respective ioSeeds list); reviewer states the role/capability link per event.
Each component lists at most 3 consumed and at most 3 produced events.
Compliant example: a component consumes an event that the owning feature's ioSeeds.consume includes.
Violation example: a component produces an event that the owning feature's ioSeeds.produce does not contain.
Component dependencies come from other components in the same feature plus external dependencies.
verification: Subset check: all consumed/produced events declared on a component must be traceable to the owning feature's ioSeeds; the checker resolves the owning feature from the plan artifact and compares the sets.

Consumed events are sourced from ioSeeds.consume filtered by the component's role and produced events from ioSeeds.produce filtered by its capability; at most 3 consumed and 3 produced events per component.
Dependency-source check: each component dependency must resolve to a component of the same feature or to an external dependency; the reference shapes for both come from the profile.

The subset check is per declared event: if the owning feature's ioSeeds list for a direction is absent or empty, any declared event in that direction is untraceable and is a finding; a component with no declared events in that direction produces no event-subset finding, but its dependencies are still checked against the dependency-source rule. No minimum number of events is required.

No automated implementation exists in the reference realization; the check is reviewer/LLM-judged until a diff-level observer over component event/dependency lists and a set-comparison checker are built. The role/capability fit of an event is a semantic judgement.
Scope: the check targets plan artifacts (which concrete artifact kinds count as plan artifacts comes from the profile); code-level changes that do not touch planning artifacts do not fire.

values: plan artifact carrying a component's consume/produce/dependency lists
plan artifact carrying a feature's ioSeeds
component consume/produce list added or edited
feature ioSeeds added, edited or removed
declared component event not in owning feature's ioSeeds
more than 3 consumed or more than 3 produced events
dependency neither same-feature component nor external
declared event not relevant to component role (consume) or capability (produce)

fires: Planner declares a component that produces an event absent from the owning feature's ioSeeds.produce.
Planner adds a consumed event to a component that the feature's ioSeeds.consume does not list.
Planner changes a feature's ioSeeds so an existing component's declared events are no longer a subset.
Planner gives a component a consumed event unrelated to its role, or a produced event unrelated to its capability.
Planner lists a fourth consumed or a fourth produced event on one component.
Planner adds a component dependency on a component of another feature that is not an external dependency.
doesNotFire: A component that declares no consumed or produced events AND whose dependencies are all same-feature components or external dependencies. (Empty event lists alone only satisfy the event-subset part; dependency sourcing must still be checked.)
Authoring a feature's ioSeeds before any component of that feature declares events or dependencies.
Code-level changes that do not touch planning artifacts.

Reference shape of a component, used to recognise a same-feature component dependency and to resolve the owning feature of a component.
The reference shape, inside a plan artifact's component dependency list, that counts as an external dependency (as opposed to a component of another feature).

proposedKeys.meaning: The reference shape, inside a plan artifact's component dependency list, that counts as an external dependency (as opposed to a component of another feature).
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: The urn group covers artifact URNs (urn.<artifact>) and file bindings (urn.binding.<artifact>) but no key describes the reference form used for external dependencies inside plan-artifact dependency lists; idiom.external_import recognises code imports of external packages, which is a different construct.

neutralityNotes: The rule's vocabulary (feature, component, ioSeeds, consume/produce, dependencies) belongs to the ATDD planning artifacts, not to any runtime stack, so it is kept verbatim in the core; 'feature.ioSeeds.consume' etc. are plan-artifact schema fields, not file paths. The 3-event cap is a methodology constant and stays in the core. What actually varies per stack — which concrete artifact kinds are plan artifacts and how component / external-dependency references are shaped — is taken from the profile (roles.plan_artifact.kinds, urn.component); accordingly the core's activation file-kind values are role-level ('plan artifact carrying a component's consume/produce/dependency lists' / '... a feature's ioSeeds') rather than the Bun kind names, and the Bun kind names are recorded as bunOnly with the profile key carrying them. The external-dependency reference shape had no existing vocabulary key and is proposed as urn.external_dependency. Concrete example events and reference ids are not repeated in the core; bun.json remains the worked reference example. 'implementation.type: none' is the Bun realization's status and is bunOnly; the core states generically that the check is reviewer/LLM-judged until a diff-level observer and set-comparison checker exist.
